bio.html:
Albert Cheung is Chief Executive Officer of BloombergNEF, a strategic research provider covering global commodities and the energy transition. He previously served as BNEF's Deputy CEO and Head of Global Transition Analysis until 2026, overseeing the firm’s coverage of clean energy, transport, industry, technology, agriculture and sustainable finance.

Albert has nearly two decades' experience in the energy transition, having joined BloombergNEF in 2009 and later held a number of leadership positions in the organization, within both research and product management. He is an internationally recognized leader and expert in the energy transition.

Albert is an engineer by training and holds a BA and MEng in Electrical and Information Engineering from the University of Cambridge.

Maria da Graça Carvalho has been Minister of Environment and Energy since 2024 (XXIV and XXV Constitutional Governments). She was Minister of Science and Higher Education in the XV Constitutional Government and Minister of Science, Innovation and Higher Education in the XVI Constitutional Government. She served two terms as a Member of the European Parliament: between 2009 and 2014, during which time she was rapporteur for the Horizon 2020 framework programme for research and innovation; and between 2019 and 2024. She was also senior advisor to the President of the European Commission, Durão Barroso, in the areas of Science, Higher Education, Innovation, Research, Energy, Environment and Climate Change (2006 to 2009) and, subsequently, advisor to the Commissioner for Research, Science and Innovation, Carlos Moedas (2012-2015). She is a member of the American Institute of Aeronautics, the American Association for the Advancement of Science, the World Academy of Art and Science, and the Portuguese Academy of Sciences. She is a Full Professor at the Instituto Superior Técnico (University of Lisbon).

Meredith is the Head of Clean Power research at BloombergNEF, a leading market research provider.

She oversees BNEF’s global coverage of solar, wind and electricity grids – and the critical role these play in the energy transition. Recent outputs include the biannual Renewable Energy Investment Tracker, Global Wind and Solar market outlooks and benchmarking grid investments relative to a net-zero path. 

Meredith has over a decade experience in the energy industry spanning power, business strategy, natural gas, carbon, hydrogen, low-carbon heating and solar. She holds a MSc in Environmental Economics and Climate Change from the London School of Economics and a BA in Economics from Williams College in Massachusetts, including an exchange at the University of Oxford.

Mr Gustin has been appointed as Chief Executive Officer Elia Group SA on January 15, 2025. He was previously Chairman of the Board of Directors of Elia Group SA, Elia Transmission Belgium SA and Elia Asset SA, a position he assumed since 2017. He served as Executive Chairman of LINEAS SA, and LINEAS Group SA. Lineas is Europe’s biggest private rail freight company. Mr. Gustin is operating advisor to DWS Infrastructure fund and in that respect is Chairman of the Board of InfraMobility a Benelux leading mobility Group and Vice Chairman of the Board of Charleroi Airport. Mr Gustin was the Co-CEO (2008-2012) and later CEO of Brussels Airlines SA/NV (2012-2018). Prior to his functions with Brussels Airlines, he was a partner with Arthur D. Little (1999-2008). Born in 1968, he holds a commercial engineering degree from ICHEC, a degree in international comparative management from ICHEC (Loyola College Maryland), and an MBA from Solvay Business School (VUB).

Abdullah is a regional transition analyst at BloombergNEF in London, primarily responsible for research on the energy transition in markets across the Middle East and North Africa, focusing on the policies, economics and technologies driving the region’s energy transition. Prior to joining BNEF, he worked for UK utility SP Energy Networks on the innovation and future networks team. Abdullah earned a master’s degree in Energy Systems from the University of Oxford and a bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering from the University of Nottingham.

Catherine Raw was appointed BHP’s Chief Development Officer in 2024. Catherine has global accountabilities for Group strategy, decision evaluation and capital planning, prioritisation and allocation, corporate business development, and mergers and acquisitions. Prior to joining BHP, Catherine held senior roles at SSE plc, Barrick Gold and BlackRock. With a background in geoscience, fund management, finance and operations, Catherine has a demonstrated track record as a strategic and commercially oriented executive able to execute growth opportunities globally.
Lola Arnold is an Analyst in the Tech and Innovation team at BloombergNEF, covering the data center market. Lola has a masters in Computer Science and Philosophy from the University of Oxford.

Dan is the Group Chief Executive of Eskom Holdings SOC Ltd, the continent’s largest power producer. Appointed in March 2024, he leads Eskom during a critical period of operational and financial performance turnaround efforts as well as the transformation of both Eskom and the electricity supply industry. With over two decades of experience in the energy and industrial sectors, he previously held other executive roles at Eskom, PetroSA, and more recently served as the Interim CEO of Tongaat Hulett, before taking on his current role as Group Chief Executive at Eskom. Dan is a seasoned turnaround expert, a charismatic and inspirational leader with a proven track record of disciplined execution in operational, strategic and change leadership roles in large organisations.

Antonio Barroso is the Europe Geoeconomics Lead, based in Geneva. He is also an adjunct professor at Science Po in Paris. Previously, he co-launched the geopolitical risk unit of consulting firm Teneo and worked as a Senior Analyst at Eurasia Group. He holds a PhD from the London School of Economics and Political Science.

Andrew Bowie was Parliamentary Under Secretary of State at the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero from 7 February 2023 to 5 July 2024.

Andrew was previously Parliamentary Under Secretary of State (Minister for Exports) at the Department for International Trade from 28 October 2022 to 7 February 2023.

He was elected the MP for West Aberdeenshire and Kincardine in 2017, making him the first Conservative MP for the seat since its creation in 1997. Andrew grew up in Aberdeenshire, and lives in the area with his wife, Maddie, baby daughter, Emily, and dalmatian puppy, Winston.

Before being elected as an MP, Andrew Bowie served as an officer in the Royal Navy for 3 years, a career that took him around the world to Brazil, Bahrain, Gibraltar and The Falklands. Returning home to the North East, Andrew studied at the University of Aberdeen before entering politics.

During his time in Parliament, Andrew has chaired the All Party Parliamentary Group for Sweden and worked as Parliamentary Private Secretary to the Prime Minister, Theresa May, (2018 to 2019), as well as Vice-Chair of the Conservative party (2019 to 2021).

profile.job_title: Shadow Secretary of State for Energy Security & Net Zero

bio.html:
Adithya was previously on BloombergNEF’s hydrogen team focusing on European hydrogen markets as well as midstream developments globally. Some of his recent work includes the 1H 2022 Hydrogen Levelized Cost Update and a techno-economic analysis of repurposed and new-build hydrogen pipelines.

Prior to BloombergNEF, Adithya worked at the University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences in Vienna analyzing the potential for hydrogen in long-haul trucking. He holds a MSc in Climate Change, Management and Finance from Imperial College London and a BSc in Ecological and Environmental Sciences with Management from University of Edinburgh.

Mag. Dr. Michael STRUGL, MBA has served as Chairman of the Managing Board of VERBUND AG, Austria's leading electricity company and one of Europe's largest hydropower electricity generators, since January 2021. His current responsibilities include corporate strategy, energy economy, business management, strategic human resources management, corporate innovation, and new business solutions, ventures, as well as marketing and communications.

https://www.linkedin.com/in/msver/

Tifenn Brandily leads the transition risk team at BloombergNEF based in London. The team focuses on the impacts of the low-carbon transition on company performance and helps investors understand policy, technology and market risks. Before this, Tifenn led BNEF’s research on low-carbon technology costs and was a key contributor to the New Energy Outlook (NEO). Tifenn holds an MSc in mechanical engineering from the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and an MA in international affairs from Sciences Po.

profile.job_title: Head of Transition Risk and Alignment Research

bio.html:
Greg Jackson CBE is the founder and CEO of Octopus Energy Group, the UK's largest energy supplier and a global energy and technology company that's driving the affordable, green energy system of the future. Octopus is innovating relentlessly to make energy better for consumers and the planet. It now serves 11 million customers globally, including 8 million in the UK, and runs rapidly expanding retail operations across France, Germany, Italy, Spain, the US, and Japan, further fueling international growth. Operating across 27 countries, the Group manages a £8 billion renewables portfolio and leads thriving businesses in EV leasing, heat pumps, and solar. It has attracted over $3 billion worth of funding from international energy companies, large pension funds and global investors. Greg is a thought leader on innovation and energy and a serial tech unicorn founder – a rare feat among British entrepreneurs. He has built two tech giants valued at billions of dollars – Octopus Energy and Kraken – as well as a number of successful businesses before starting Octopus. He is also an angel investor in a wide range of start-ups. In 2024, Greg was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) and named one of TIME magazine's 100 Most Influential Climate Leaders. He was appointed a Non-Executive Member of the Cabinet Office Board in 2025.

linkedin.com/in/gregsjackson

Tasneem Hanfi Brogger is Bloomberg's Managing Editor for ESG and Green in EMEA, a role that's seen her lead reporting on the intersection of finance, regulation, and sustainability across the region. Her team's current focus is all the ways in which themes like energy security, defense, and geopolitics are reshaping ESG and climate strategies inside the finance industry, and how this development feeds into broader themes of politics and financial stability.

Before running Bloomberg's ESG and Green coverage in EMEA, Tasneem was Managing Editor for the Nordic region. She's an Australian and Danish national, with degrees in finance and music.

profile.job_title: Managing Editor, ESG and Green in EMEA

bio.html:
Natalie Blyth is Global Head of Sustainable Finance & Transition at HSBC. She is also a Non-Executive Director on the HSBC Latin America Holdings Board.


Natalie has a 30-year career in banking, with extensive global leadership experience spanning investment banking, client coverage, trade and sustainable finance, and an exceptional track record in building high-impact, commercially successful teams.


In 2022, she was appointed head of HSBC’s global Commercial Banking Sustainability business, where she delivered material profitable revenue growth, contributed to HSBC’s #1 global Euromoney Sustainable Finance award, and was recognised as a top ten women leader in sustainability. Prior to this, Natalie led HSBC’s Global Trade & Receivables Finance business, establishing the bank as a market leader in trade finance.
She is passionate about working with clients to help them navigate the complexities of sustainability and achieve their transition priorities with safe, sustainable, profitable growth.


She has a Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry with Mathematics and Bioenergetics from the University of St Andrews in Scotland.

Linkedin

profile.job_title: Global Head of Sustainable Finance & Transition

bio.html:
Nayel is a corporate energy analyst and is part of BNEF’s solar team. He joined the company in May 2024. His research focuses on corporate clean energy procurement. This involves tracking global corporate power purchase agreements and helping corporations, developers and investors understand market dynamics and corporate progress on their decarbonization targets.

Prior to joining Bloomberg, Nayel completed an MSc in Climate Change, Management and Finance from Imperial College London, and a BSc in International Business, Finance and Economics from the University of Manchester. Upon completion of his studies, he worked as a commercial sustainability consultant on European sustainability regulation compliance, Scope 1 and 2 decarbonization.

Cathy McClay is Managing Director of National Grid DSO and Great Britain's first Flexibility Commissioner. With more than 25 years' experience across energy trading, system operation and market design, she has worked at the heart of some of the most significant changes in the electricity sector. Her career has included opening flexibility markets to new technologies in Great Britain and developing the markets and systems needed to balance NEOM's fully renewable energy network in Saudi Arabia. Cathy is a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering and was awarded an OBE for services to the energy sector.

Emma Champion is Head of Regional Energy Transitions at BloombergNEF, leading analysis of long-term decarbonization scenarios for energy in Europe and Africa. Her research focus areas include clean energy policy and investment, power markets, electrification, and industrial decarbonization.

Emma holds a Master's degree from the University of Oxford in Global Governance and Diplomacy with a focus on climate policy, and a certificate in Sustainable Finance from the University of Cambridge Institute for Sustainability Leadership. She is also currently serving a three-year term as an Expert Member to the European Commission's Investors Dialogue for Energy on behalf of BloombergNEF.

Declan Burke is Nuclear Power Strategy Director at Centrica, where he leads the company's work on its nuclear strategy. Centrica has a range of interests across the nuclear sector, including existing generation, new build and advanced reactor opportunities, with a particular focus on the role of firm low-carbon power in supporting energy security, industrial growth and the rising power demand associated with AI. Before joining Centrica, Declan was Director of Group Strategy at SSE. Prior to that he spent almost a decade in senior government roles, including as Director for Nuclear Projects and Director for Clean Power Strategy, helping shape UK energy and nuclear policy. He also served as a Non-Executive Director of the Low Carbon Contracts Company. Earlier in his career, Declan worked in investment banking and the Shareholder Executive, advising on major infrastructure and corporate transactions.

Sarah Wells is a Senior Executive Editor at Bloomberg News, where she oversees a global team of approximately 180 journalists covering commodities and energy, climate, equality, and management.

Currently based in London, Sarah was previously Co-Head of News for the Asia-Pacific region, based in Singapore. She began her career at a business newspaper in her native New Zealand before joining Bloomberg in Sydney in 2009. Since then, she has held a variety of reporting, editing, and management roles, specializing in credit, equities, and other financial markets.

Sarah holds a Bachelor's degree in Communication Studies from Auckland University of Technology and is a CFA Charterholder.

Felicitas is the Director of the Innovation and Competitiveness Department at the EIB’s Projects Directorate (since Feb. 2022). She oversees technical and economic due diligence of EIB’s projects in R&D-intensive sectors, including CRM, automotive, pharmaceutical, and telecom industries, as well as education, health, and digital infrastructures. In her department projects from the public and private sector are covered benefitting from the entire range of financial products offered by EIB. Before this role, she was the Head of the Life Science and Health Division, which she joined in 2007 as a Life Science Specialist. In this capacity, she was responsible for the life sciences, pharmaceutical, and health sectors. A key achievement during her tenure was successfully leading the team through the COVID-19 pandemic, positioning EIB as a strong partner in the sector by establishing critical partnerships with organizations such as the World Health Organization (WHO), the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF), and the Wellcome Trust. Before joining the EIB, Felicitas worked at the European Investment Fund as an Investment Manager, focusing on technology transfer. Her main tasks included analyzing technology transfer, developing financial instruments targeting this area, and implementing these funding structures. Prior to that, she worked as a strategy consultant for L.E.K. Consulting in Munich and Los Angeles, where she focused on Private Equity, M&A, and Life Sciences, handling business planning, market research, and development of market entry strategies, as well as financial and commercial due diligence. Felicitas holds a Master of Science from Philipps University of Marburg with a major in human genetics and molecular biology and was a visiting researcher at Stanford University in Palo Alto. She recently completed the Advanced Management Program (AMP) at Harvard Business School in Boston.

Jenny Chase is an analyst with BloombergNEF’s global Solar Insight Service. She joined BNEF mid-2005 and launched the Solar Insight Service in early 2006, and ran the team from Bloomberg's Zurich office until late 2022. She then stepped down from management and continues to write about and analyse the solar industry as part of the team.

Jenny has conducted or overseen most of the research of the Solar Insight Service since 2006, and is the lead author of BNEF’s quarterly Global PV Market Outlook.


Jenny is the author of a book, Solar Power Finance Without the Jargon, published by World Scientific Publishing in 2019. She holds a BA in Physical Sciences and an MSci in Physics from the University of Cambridge, England, and breeds award-winning West of England geese. She is on Twitter as @solar_chase and Mastodon as solar_chase@mastodon.green.

Dr. Matthias Dohrn is President of Global Procurement at BASF, where he leads the company's global sourcing and procurement activities. Throughout his career at BASF, Dr. Dohrn has made contributions in areas such as finance, precious metal services, and battery base metals and recycling. He has gained valuable insights into various markets and industries through his work in Germany, South Africa, and the United States. Dr. Dohrn completed his studies in Economics at the Westfälische Wilhelms-Universität Münster and earned a doctorate in Economics from Leibniz University Hannover in 2004.

Victoria is Head of Global Policy at BloombergNEF – Bloomberg’s primary research service covering clean energy, advanced transport, digital industry and innovative materials. Having joined the company in 2009, she has written reports on a wide range of topics, including government responses to declining fuel tax revenue, risk-mitigation mechanisms for renewables projects, carbon markets, local content requirements, small modular reactors, heat decarbonization, power markets in the Middle East and North Africa, and the implications of Brexit. Before BNEF, Victoria spent four years as an editor working with the European Commission and Parliament in Brussels; and for an economics consultancy in Oxford. She holds two Master’s degrees from the University of Cambridge, and another Master’s from the University of Durham.

Aude Beuter leads Green Energy Acceleration at ENGIE's Supply & Energy Management division, scaling green energy activities across 20 platforms — ENGIE ranks #1 worldwide for Power Purchase Agreements, with 3.6 GW signed in 2025 (BNEF). She sets standards and monitors performance across the portfolio, challenging management teams on commercial strategy, market positioning and profitability drivers. An engineer by training with a decade in strategy consulting, she brings a rigorous, results-oriented lens to the PPA market's current price tensions and flexibility challenges.

Mark Daly is Head of Technology and Innovation at BloombergNEF. He covers financing, technology, and policy trends for commercializing the next generation of sustainable industrial technologies. Mark holds an MSc in Climate Change, Management and Finance from Imperial College and a Bachelor's Degree in Mathematics from Trinity College Dublin.

profile.job_title: Head of Data Centers & Emerging Technologies

bio.html:
Tony is the firm's Founding Partner & Group Chief Executive Officer, based in the firm’s London headquarters. He is responsible for the firm’s governance, management, and strategy, as well as origination, transaction negotiation, structuring, and overall company development activities within the management team.

Before Tower Peak, Anthony was a co-Founder and CEO of Victory Hill Capital Partners LLP, where he was responsible for firm governance, management, strategy, and portfolio management of the firm’s $530mn London-listed fund (ticker: GSEO LN) focused on global sustainable energy investments.

Prior to this, he was responsible for international business strategy and private asset investments globally, as well as institutional investment solutions for EMEA, and helped build and develop the real asset investment business of Asset Management One Alternative Investments, the alternative asset management arm of Mizuho Financial Group. He was also a founding principal of Mizuho Bank’s Energy Special Situations Group and was involved in various private capital markets transactions with the investment banking sector.

Prior to this, he was a Partner at AlphaOne Partners LLP in their energy-focused private equity business, where he contributed to building industrial partnerships with global industrial energy groups.

He also worked for Goldman Sachs as an Executive Director, where he was responsible for financial institutions strategy and strategic relationships with institutional investors across Europe and the United States.

Before Goldman Sachs, he worked in both equity and fixed-income derivatives at Credit Suisse, Deutsche Bank, and ABN AMRO.

He began his career as a Statistics Research Analyst at the European Central Bank in Frankfurt.

Prior to banking, he spent some time working in the directorate for foreign affairs of the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium, where he worked on the Euromed Trade Agreement.

He holds a BA (Hons) in Management & Business Administration from Henley Business School, an MSc in Global Politics from the University of Southampton, and an MBA from the University of Cambridge.

He is a member of the UK CFA Institute. He is also a Freeman of the Worshipful Company of International Bankers, a Fellow of the Energy Institute, and a regular financial industry guest speaker at the Judge School of Business at the University of Cambridge.

profile.job_title: Founding Partner & Group Chief Executive Officer

bio.html:
Ryan is a specialist in the electrified transport team at BloombergNEF. He covers the technology, policy and economic factors shaping the transport sector. Within the team Ryan author’s research on electric vehicles and charging infrastructure.

Prior to joining BloombergNEF Ryan worked at Jaguar Land Rover for five years working on their electrification and mobility strategies. This included leading on the end of life strategy for EV batteries, completing projects on EV charging, the launch of electric vehicles and the creation of InMotion. A subsidiary which invests in new mobility businesses. Ryan holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Liverpool University and a Masters Degree in Automotive Technology from the University of Warwick.

Alex Grant has over 25 years of experience in global energy markets, investment banking, and strategic leadership. He currently serves as Senior Vice President and Global Head of Crude, Products & Liquids Trading at Equinor, where he is also the UK Country Manager. In this dual role Alex is responsible for leading Equinor's strategic presence in the UK across the energy space as well as handling liquids trading globally.

Alex joined Equinor in 2017 as Senior Vice President for Global Business Development. In that capacity, he led the company’s mergers, acquisitions, and divestments across its oil, gas, and renewables portfolios, playing a key role in shaping Equinor’s transition strategy and global growth.

Prior to joining Equinor, Alex spent over two decades in investment banking at JP Morgan, ABN AMRO and Jefferies, where he specialised in M&A and capital markets transactions within the energy sector.

Chris is the Head of Nuclear Research at BloombergNEF. He directs the firm's nuclear energy research team, developing a robust methodology for forecasting global nuclear investment in new build, innovative technologies, O&M, fuel cycle and decommissioning.

In this capacity, Chris has worked closely with Nuclear Matters, a coalition that informs the public and policymakers about the benefits of nuclear energy, and with the International Framework for Nuclear Energy Cooperation, a forum of 34 participant and 31 observer countries that explores beneficial approaches to ensure the use of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

As a business development and corporate communications consultant prior to joining BloombergNEF, Chris worked with regional and multinational firms and global institutions on energy and environment projects. Past clients include the United Nations Development Program, World Bank, U.S. Department of Energy, and UNDP/Global Environment Facility. Chris has worked on energy project development in the Middle East and in California, and was invited as an "energy leader" to explore renewable energy and technology transfer business opportunities in Israel in 2009.

Chris joined the faculty of New York University's Center for Global Affairs in September 2005 where he teaches graduate courses on Energy Policy, The Economics and Finance of Energy, and Nuclear Energy. Current research interests include the social, technical, economic, environmental and political challenges to nuclear and renewable energy development.

Chris has published extensively on energy and power generation topics in: Modern Power Systems, EuroMoney/ Institutional Investor's Project Finance Magazine, Nuclear Engineering International, The China Business Review, and Independent Energy Magazine. Following the March 11, 2011 magnitude 9.0 earthquake and ensuing tsunami, Chris discussed the implications of the Fukushima nuclear event as a guest on Bloomberg TV, MSNBC, National Public Radio, and ABC and CBS affiliates. 

Chris earned a MBA in Market Management from the Zicklin School of Business, Baruch College/CUNY, a MS from the Brooklyn Polytechnic University, and a BA from the College of the Holy Cross.

Devrim is the Chief Flexibility and Marketing Officer at Kraken. Overseeing Kraken’s flexibility and product capabilities, the cloud-based flexibility platform controls and optimizes distributed energy resources such as batteries of all sizes, EVs, solar and wind generation or heat pumps with machine learning and AI to match electricity supply and demand, helping the electricity grid deal with the natural volatility of renewable generation. Kraken is currently shifting over 15GWh or load per day. Devrim is also responsible for Kraken’s market development and expansion into new regions.

Previously, Devrim was the CEO of Upside Energy, which was acquired by Kraken in 2020. Before starting Upside Energy, Devrim’s professional career saw him take up executive roles with blue chip management consultancies and finance companies such as Publicis Sapient, Kearney and Lansdowne. He also holds an MBA from Yale University. In 2023, Devrim joined the Elexon Board, which manages the Balancing and Settlement Code of Great Britain’s energy system, as a Non-Executive Director.

Ellie Gomes-Callus is a Metals and Mining Associate at BloombergNEF. Her research covers battery metal markets, global critical mineral policies and the pathways to decarbonization for the mining sector. Prior to her role at BloombergNEF, Ellie spent her time as a Research Scientist with RFC Power, an energy storage start up, before joining the UK Government. At the Department of Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy, she worked in oil and gas policy and energy innovation funding. Ellie holds a BSc in Natural Sciences from the University of Nottingham and a MRes in Green Chemistry from Imperial College London

Ann is VP - PPA & BESS Transaction Advisory at Pexapark, the price intelligence platform for clean energy. Over more than 13 years originating structured power contracts for tier-1 utilities, she has negotiated long-term power offtake agreements and advised corporate and utility clients on managing energy price risk across volatile power markets. Since joining Pexapark in 2022, she has closed both upstream and downstream PPAs across Central Western Europe, Poland, and the Nordics, and worked extensively with flexible assets - experience directly relevant to today's hybrid PPA structures. Ann began her career as a Merchant Banking Management Trainee at Fortis Bank, after a master's in Engineering & Trade Economics from the Vrije Universiteit Brussel.

profile.job_title: Vice President - PPA & BESS Transaction Advisory

bio.html:
Andrew Grant is a head of intelligent mobility at BloombergNEF.

He produces analysis on business models, technologies and policies related to connected cars, mobility services and autonomous driving. Andrew works with automakers, utilities, technology companies and investors to understand the role of data in the future of transportation.

Amit Gudka is the Founder and CEO of Field, a leading European vertically integrated battery energy storage company developing, building, and operating BESS assets across the UK, Germany, Italy, and Spain, with a growing focus on long-duration energy storage.

Before Field, Amit founded the energy supplier Bulb and prior to that was an energy trader at Barclays, focussed on European power and gas markets.

Matthew Hales is a research analyst at BloombergNEF specializing in trade policy and clean-technology industrial strategies of economies around the world. He is focused on industrial strategies that affect solar, battery, electric vehicle and wind manufacturing and trade, with a particular interest in emerging markets opportunities.

Matthew sits within BloombergNEF's Trade & Supply Chains team, and is based in London. He has former experience analyzing the creditworthiness of debt issued by entities linked to governments, and holds a M.A in Economic History from the University of Edinburgh.

Bianca is a Managing Director at CPP Investments’ Sustainable Energies Group and is responsible for originating, executing and managing power and distributed energy investments in Europe.

Prior to joining CPP Investments in 2017, Bianca worked at Santander’s proprietary investments team (currently known as Cubico Sustainable Investments) focused on investing in renewable energy in Brazil. Before that, Bianca worked at Patria Investments, a Brazilian private equity firm, and Citibank.

Bianca holds a BBus (Hons) from Fundação Getulio Vargas in Brazil, an MBA from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, and an MA from the Lauder Institute at the University of Pennsylvania.

Lara Hayim leads BNEF’s solar research team and has been with the company since February 2016. During her time as a solar analyst, she focused on operations and maintenance, performance of solar power plants, solar-plus-storage projects and solar markets of Europe and Middle East.

She completed a BA in Economics from the Bosphorous University in Turkey followed by an MSc in Environment and Development from the University of Edinburgh. Upon completion of her studies, Lara worked as a consultant, working with private and public sector clients on renewable energy capacity studies with a particular focus on the solar markets. She also brings her experience of developing solar projects through her role in a social housing provider in the UK, where she worked for two years prior to joining BNEF. Lara speaks fluent Turkish and English.

profile.job_title: Head of Clean Power Revenues & Finance

bio.html:
Sana Khareghani is the Chief Strategy Officer at Era4, an AI infrastructure company delivering resilient, lower-carbon, high-performance compute capacity to support the UK’s AI transformation. She is also Professor of Practice in AI at King’s College London and AI Policy Lead for Responsible AI UK, a £35 million programme supporting research and innovation in responsible AI. Sana has over 25 years of experience across technology, business, and public policy in both the private and public sectors. She has worked as a software engineer in large corporations and start-ups, as a management consultant advising C-suite leaders internationally, and in government as the inaugural Head of the UK Government Office for AI, where she led the team that published the UK’s National AI Strategy and supported £1 billion of investment in the UK AI ecosystem.

Linkedin

Alice He is an Associate in the Energy Systems Modeling team at BloombergNEF, where she focuses on global data center demand forecasting and long-term electricity demand modeling. She contributes to BloombergNEF’s flagship New Energy Outlook, examining the impact of rising electricity demand on power systems and decarbonization pathways.

Alice holds an MPhil in Economics from the University of Oxford and a BA in Mathematics and Economics from New York University.

Dr. Tim Heidel is Co-Founder & Chief Executive Officer at VEIR. Tim served as VEIR’s first Chief Technology Officer from January 2020 when the company was founded until February 2023. Prior to VEIR, Tim was a member of the investments team at Breakthrough Energy Ventures (BEV), investing in companies that leverage innovative technologies to significantly address climate change. He served as Deputy Chief Scientist at the National Rural Electric Cooperative Association (NRECA), where he helped lead technology scouting and research and development activities on behalf of the 900 non-profit, member-owned electric utility members. He served as a Fellow and Program Director at the Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy (ARPA-E), leading the development of 3 new programs and managed a portfolio of over 75 research projects, focusing on approaches for controlling and optimizing the transmission and delivery of electric power and managing programs focused on high-efficiency power electronics.

https://www.linkedin.com/in/timheidel/

Jess is a weather analyst at BloombergNEF, where she monitors forecasts and historical trends to uncover how weather shapes risks and opportunities across power and energy markets. Before joining BloombergNEF, she assessed weather influences on agricultural risk, focusing on global cereal and oilseed production impacts. With a background in paleoclimatology from the University of Michigan and a Master’s in climate modelling from the University of Leeds, Jess draws on both historical and predictive insights at the intersection of weather, climate and commodities.

Sam is Director of Energy at Climate Group. He has 30 years’ experience, driving systemic change in the energy, transport and construction sectors.

He leads the energy work at Climate Group, accelerating the global roll out of renewables and energy efficiency measures, through the RE100 initiative, EP100 energy efficiency initiative, and the 24/7 Carbon Free Coalition.

Prior to joining Climate Group, Sam spearheaded Forum for the Future’s Sustainable Shipping Initiative, which won the Guardian Sustainable Business Award for innovative consultancy.

Sam has a MSc in Pollution and Environmental Control from the University of Manchester and a BSc in Natural Environmental Science from Sheffield University.

Layla is an associate, Carbon Credits and Environmental Markets at BloombergNEF. Her research focuses on carbon offsets and the voluntary carbon market. This involves helping corporations, traders and investors understand the market, and the role carbon offsets play in achieving corporate net-zero targets. Layla holds an MSc in Energy Systems from the University of Oxford, and a BSc in Mechanical Engineering from the American University of Sharjah.

profile.job_title: Associate, Carbon Credits and Environmental Markets

bio.html: Richard König is co-founder, shareholder and CEO of Enery, an independent renewable power producer focused on Austria and CEE. Enery is a purpose-driven company with an aim to provide affordable, reliable, clean and sustainable electricity to industrial customers and households in the region. Before founding Enery in 2019, Richard led the growth and renewable transformation of ContourGlobal, an American IPP. Before that, after studying Economics and Business at Graz University, he worked in renewable energy investment banking in London, Amsterdam and CEE. Next to Enery, Richard is shareholder in other companies in the energy, agriculture and sports business. He is passionate about supporting local communities in CEE with social projects and has executed more than 15 of such initiatives over the last years.

Jonathan Luan is the Head of Finance and Investment Research for BloombergNEF, based in London. He leads BNEF’s global coverage on the climate transition of banks, asset managers and asset owners, and the opportunities and gaps in energy transition finance and investment. He has a decade of experience in coal and renewable energy policy, power market and economics, and corporate sustainability. BNEF is a strategic research provider covering global commodity markets and the disruptive technologies driving the transition to a low-carbon economy. Jonathan holds a master's degree from the George Washington University in Washington, D.C.

Shreya Malik (London) joined KKR in 2021 and is a Managing Director on the Infrastructure team. She currently serves on the Board of Directors of Zenobe and was previously a member of the Board of Directors of Refresco. Prior to joining KKR, Ms. Malik spent over a decade at Partners Group, most recently as senior vice president on Partners Group's infrastructure team, where she was responsible for originating and executing transactions across Europe. Sofia Maia leads BloombergNEF’s Country Transition and Middle East & Africa Research team, based in London. She oversees research on how emerging markets are advancing the global shift toward a low-carbon economy, with in-depth country and regional analysis across the Middle East and Africa. Sofia also manages the Global Climatescope project, BloombergNEF’s flagship assessment of energy transition progress and investment attractiveness across more than 90 emerging markets worldwide. She holds a degree in Public Administration from Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV – São Paulo).

Progressive is also developing other clusters including the Peak Cluster, Bacton, and early stage developments in Ireland and Scandinavia  Irish cluster and  and an early stage cluster in Ireland. Chris has sits on a number of Advisory Boards, including the DESNZ Science and Technology Advisory Council and the Energy Minister’s Hydrogen Delivery Council.

Caitilín McManus is a Technology Analyst at BloombergNEF. She covers data center supply chains, with a focus in power systems, cooling, and energy storage. Caitilín holds a PhD in Chemistry from the University of Oxford and previously worked as a researcher for the French Centre for Alternative Energy.

Ivo Prokopiev is Founder and CEO of Renalfa Solarpro Group (Renalfa), a Vienna-based, vertically integrated clean energy and e-mobility group operating across Central and Eastern Europe.

Renalfa is one of the largest independent clean energy groups in CEE. The group pioneered long-duration battery storage and hybrid renewable business models in Europe, and today owns over 1.5 GW of operational hybrid RES assets and 3.6 GWh of batteries. It is supplying over 4.5 TWh of green energy annually to exchanges, industry and households in four countries, throughout its power trading firm - Toki.

Its EV charging network Eldrive and car-sharing platform Spark are also market leaders in the region, with over 4000 operating charging points and c. 2,000 shared EVs.

Mr. Prokopiev holds a Master’s in Finance from the University of National and World Economy in Sofia, and an EMBA from INSEAD.

Oliver Metcalfe is Strategic Lead for European Research at BloombergNEF, where he works across regional, sector and commodities research teams to strengthen BNEF’s coverage of the European energy transition. He supports clients navigating the policy, market and technology shifts reshaping energy systems across the region.

Oliver has worked across BNEF’s New York and London offices and previously led the firm’s global wind research practice for four years. Before joining BNEF, he worked at the Energy Industries Council, providing data and market intelligence for UK clean energy supply chain companies. Oliver holds an MSc in Environmental Technology from Imperial College London.

Professor Ellen Quigley is the Director of Finance for Systemic Change and a Research Professor at the University of Cambridge whose work focuses on building the intellectual and practical foundations of a more sustainable and equitable financial system. To this end, she convenes and advises some of the world’s largest and most influential asset owners to confront and reshape systemic risks such as climate change and inequality through their investment and stewardship policies and practices. Her widely-deployed framework, “Universal Ownership in Practice” – which received the GRASFI Paper Prize for Potential Impact on Sustainable Finance Practices – provides a practical guide for asset owners to deliver real-world outcomes in service of a stable long-term financial system. A forthcoming book building on this work will be published in 2026 by Cambridge University Press as part of its Elements in Corporate Governance series.

Maia Mésanger is a research specialist leading BloombergNEF’s global coverage on sustainable finance policy and covering transition risk. She was part of the European Commission’s Platform on Sustainable Finance up until October 2022, supporting Nadia Humphreys, then a Bloomberg member and rapporteur for the expert group. Maia holds a bachelor’s degree in philosophy from Université Pierre Mendes France, as well as two master’s degrees in management and finance from Grenoble Ecole de Management.

profile.job_title: Specialist, Sustainable Finance Policy & Transition Risk

bio.html:
Federica Sabbati is Secretary General of the European Heating Industry, which brings together companies that are leaders in the production of efficient heating systems. EHI gathers 40 European market leaders producing heating systems and 13 national heating associations. As such they cover close to 80% of the European market of heat pumps (electric, hybrid, thermally driven) and 90% of the market of all heating solutions - from boilers to solar thermal systems, green gas- heating appliances (boilers, fuel cells, micro-CHP) to pumps and circulators, from radiators or underfloor heat emitters.

Under her leadership EHI has developed the EHI proprietary market data collection methodology that has become the industry reference for regular heat pumps and heating market data trends. The heating market intelligence activities of the EHI expand to cover from Western to Central and Eastern Europe as well as international markets such as China. Recently, the association has increased further market intelligence initiatives on nascent trends in heat pumps deployment (hybrids, heat pumps segmentations by type, use, refrigerant etc).

In 2020 EHI launched the first European Heating Market Report , which provides the largest data set available on the European heating market (both on installed stock and annual sales for several heating technologies) and is a regular EHI publication.

Federica holds a university degree in International Relations from the University of Trieste, Italy, and a Master’s Degree in Russian and Post-Soviet Studies from the London School of Economics and Political Science in the UK.

Tara leads the Upstream Oil analysis team at BNEF. The team covers global oil production and breakeven costs, the lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions of production and methane leakages, as well as the hedging strategies of US oil producers.

In Tara’s time at BNEF, she led BNEF’s US long term decarbonization analysis, looking at cross sectoral trends, analyzed US power markets with a focus on PJM, and produced medium term outlooks for renewables. Her research has covered economic, policy and company trends in the US. Prior to BNEF, she was a manufacturing engineer at Ford.

Tara holds an MS in Natural Resources and Environment and an MA in Applied Economics from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, and a B.Tech Mechatronics Engineering from SASTRA University, India.

Experienced sustainability professional with over 10 years’ experience in stewardship, ESG integration, and climate strategy across asset management and public policy. Previously she worked four years at Royal London Asset Management, in stewardship and integration of climate change. Furthermore, her work experience includes roles at the Green Finance Institute and Oxford University Net Zero research group and five years at the British Embassy in Caracas, leading their Sustainability and Energy work. She graduated with distinction in a Master of Science on Environmental Change and Management at the University of Oxford. She also holds a Master’s in Public Administration and a Hydrocarbon Management Graduate Diploma.

Nelson has a background conducting investment research on private companies across Sub-Saharan African markets and joined BNEF from research firm Asoko Insight. He holds an MSc in Finance from Trinity College Dublin and a BSc in Accounting and Finance from the University of Kent.

Stefano Terranova is the Chief Executive Officer of Atlante, a leading electric mobility player in Southern Europe. Appointed in October 2021, Stefano has led the creation of Atlante from scratch: developing the organizational structure and recruiting a talented team to execute ambitious growth plans across Europe. Atlante now operates in Italy, France, Spain, and Portugal, with over 3,000 charging points online in 1000+ stations. Stefano’s leadership has been crucial in establishing Atlante as a key player in the European electric vehicle fast charging infrastructure market. He has spearheaded partnerships with major entities such as Stellantis, Mastercard, and the French Government’s CDC, among others. Under his direction, Atlante has achieved significant milestones, including securing €90 million in EU grants under the CEF Transport program, winning public and private tenders across four countries and most importantly setting up a full digital tech and platform to operate its stations.

Before setting up Atlante, Stefano held senior leadership roles at ENGIE, where he served as Head of Acquisitions, Investments, and Financial Advisory (AIFA) for Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. During this time, he contributed to the development of renewable energy portfolios and led complex financing projects that raised over USD 20 billion in capital. His experience also includes a top leadership position at AMEA Power, roles in investment banking with Credit Agricole in London and senior management positions with International Power Plc (a then FTSE100 company).


Stefano holds a Master’s of Science in Economics and Finance from the University of York and a degree in Economics and Commerce from the University of Rome, where he graduated with honors. He is also a CFA® charterholder. Stefano is married with two daughters, and in his free time, he enjoys entertaining friends, traveling, reading and the outdoors.

Rose is a Senior Associate in the Renewable Fuels team at BloombergNEF, based in London. Sofia Perelli-Rocco is an Associate covering Europe’s energy transition at BloombergNEF, based in London. Her cross-sector research focuses primarily on power and renewable energy markets in Central and Eastern Europe, with additional coverage of Italy, Germany, Greece, Poland and Romania.

She analyzes market trends, policy developments, auction design and investment economics, and publishes an annual report on the key energy-transition trends shaping Central and Eastern Europe.

At BloombergNEF, Sofia advises corporates, policymakers and financial institutions on European power and energy-storage markets. Her work includes assessing renewable and storage auctions, evaluating project returns and cost dynamics, and examining how European energy and industrial policies affect market development.

Before joining BloombergNEF, Sofia worked at Snam, where she assessed hydrogen technologies and supported M&A and venture investment opportunities. She also worked at EF Solare Italia, conducting techno-economic analysis of battery and hydrogen storage solutions.

Working closely with the Abra CEO, senior leadership teams, and the Board, she drives alignment across the Group’s airline brands, supports disciplined execution, and strengthens data, controls, and reporting to meet evolving regulatory, market and stakeholder expectations. Her role focuses on overseeing material ESG risks and opportunities, supporting long term value creation, and enabling consistent implementation while respecting local operating and regulatory requirements.

María has more than 20 years of experience across sustainability, strategy, and finance. Based out of Houston, Ashish leads a global group of energy, commodities and technology sector experts analyzing net-zero emissions pathways. He works extensively with CXOs & policy makers to decipher the inter-dependencies between various components of the energy transition, to facilitate strategic decision-making.

His team analyses asset valuations and investments, financing and contractual structures, technology evolution, policy developments and demand-supply drivers in power, natural gas & LNG, oil & petrochemicals, metals & mining, biofuels, and carbon markets.

In his previous role as the Head of Asia Pacific Research at BloombergNEF in Singapore, he also analyzed and advised on renewable energy, battery storage, sustainable finance, and mobility sectors.

Over the years Ashish has spoken at leading forums such as the World Future Energy Summit, World Energy Leader’s Summit and the Clean Energy Ministerial, hosted dialogues with G-20 ministers and given inputs to the works of the World Economic Forum and the World Energy Council. He has also shared his views at the London Stock Exchange, the White House executive office and at leading educational institutions.

Prior to joining Bloomberg, he led digital technology, capital budgeting and business process re-engineering projects across the world at European and Indian business consulting and technology firms. Ashish started his career at one of India’s largest private sector power companies where he oversaw commercial operations and smart grid deployment. An alumnus of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kanpur, he has a first-class degree in Engineering and an MBA in Finance and Strategy. Ashish is also a graduate of the Harvard Business School’s Advanced Management Program.

Wenjing Xiao is a global strategy and investment executive with nearly 20 years of experience driving growth, transformation, and value creation across the energy and technology sectors in Europe, North America, and Asia.

Before joining Schneider Electric, Wenjing advised on and executed major investments and transactions at ENGIE, focusing on renewable energy, hydrogen, and sustainable mobility. She began her career in business advisory at Ernst & Young in China.

Kristian Ruby is a widely recognised expert with a strong communication profile and extensive experience in political affairs. He joined Eurelectric from Wind Europe, where he served as Chief Policy Officer and was in charge of development and implementation of the political strategy.

Prior to this, Ruby worked as a journalist and served seven years as a public servant in the Danish Ministries of Environment, and Climate and Energy and in the European Commission in the cabinet of the former Climate Action chief, Connie Hedegaard.

Kristian holds a master degree in history and international development.

Yara is an analyst at BloombergNEF, where she leads the firm’s research on the decarbonization of buildings, with a focus on residential and industrial heat pumps. Her work explores technology adoption, investment flows and system impacts, benchmarked against fossil fuel alternatives.

She previously spent a summer in BNEF's Energy Economics team, researching low-carbon dispatchable power technologies including CCS in power, hydrogen-fired turbines, and small modular nuclear reactors.

She joined BNEF following a PhD in chemistry, combining academic work on bismuth catalysts for CO2 and H2 activation with an industry-funded project on semiconductor materials.

Konrad Hanschmidt, leveraging his extensive background in electricity markets, co-founded Gridio in 2018. The company originated from the insight that smart demand management could significantly benefit both EV owners and the energy grid by synchronizing vehicle charging with optimal energy conditions. This approach addresses the increasing strain on grids posed by widespread EV adoption while offering cost savings to consumers.

Gridio unlocks EV flexibility for energy suppliers. The company works directly with 10 car company brands to forecast, measure and steer their charging according to energy suppliers portfolio needs. This can be in the form of regular tariff optimisation through their EV smart charging app, or portfolio flexibility on day-ahead or intraday markets. The company’s vision is to seamlessly integrate electric cars and homes into the future energy system, fostering a more sustainable and efficient energy landscape.

Cosmo is a solar and storage analyst at BloombergNEF. He covers co-located renewables globally. His latest research focuses on tax credit policy in the US.

Prior to BNEF, Cosmo worked in the finance sector. He holds an MSc in Sustainability from the University of Oxford.

Caspar’s previously worked in a number of financial stability roles at the Bank of England – including as a senior manager in the field of macroprudential policy, in prudential policy, and in bank resolution. Between 2020 and 2022, Caspar worked for a global asset manager in the field of sustainable investing.

bio.html: Peter is the Head of Grids and Utilities analysis at BloombergNEF, leading the firm's global coverage on the investment, regulation, supply chains, new technologies and digital solutions required for our ageing power transmission and distribution networks to rise to the challenge of increasing levels of renewable energy and electricity demand. Our recent outputs include our annual Power Grid Investment Outlook and analysis of supply chain constraints in Europe and the US, the emergence of grid stability markets and the bold plans for new grid interconnection in the US. Prior to joining BNEF, Peter worked in the grids industry for over a decade with roles spanning across academic research, renewable connection studies, transmission system operation and planning, and grid software development. André is Managing Director within JPMorgan's Centre for Carbon Transition (CCT). CCT has a global mandate to provide clients with centralized access to transition-focused financing, research and advisory solutions. CCT also engages clients on their long-term business strategies and related carbon disclosures. André co-lead the development and implementation of JPMorgan’s Carbon Compass Methodology whereby the firm set its net zero targets. He was recently part of the expert group advising on the Transition Finance Market Review, a U.K. government commissioned initiative developed to examine barriers and solutions to unlocking transition finance at scale.

André was global head of Environmental and Social Risk Management at JPMorgan in London for 10 years, guiding the assessment of environmental and social issues associated with a broad range of banking transactions.

André was previously Director at Sustainable Finance Ltd., focusing on the delivery of environmental and social risk management services to the financial sector. Prior to joining Sustainable Finance, André was head of Sustainable Business Advisory within ABN AMRO Bank's risk management division in Amsterdam, where he co-authored the Equator Principles and led the implementation efforts within ABN AMRO.

André chaired the Hydropower Sustainability Assessment Forum, a multi-stakeholder initiative of the International Hydropower Association, which proposed revisions to the industry's sustainability protocol.

Henrik Juhl Hansen is Managing Director of Vaillant Group UK & Ireland and a senior industry leader at the forefront of shaping the energy transition, with more than 30 years of international leadership experience across the USA, Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

Since joining Vaillant Group in 2016, Henrik has played a key role in the company’s organisational and commercial transition towards low carbon heating technologies. He has led the business across multiple European markets before taking on responsibility for the UK and Ireland in 2022, where he now oversees one of Vaillant Group’s most strategically important regions.

Under his leadership, Vaillant and Glow-worm have accelerated their investment in and commitment to the heating transition, including the development of a new £40m manufacturing facility in Derby to support heat pump deployment. His approach reflects Vaillant’s ambition to combine innovation with practicality, whilst ensuring high quality, reliable heating solutions remain accessible for consumers and deliverable at scale. Henrik is a strong advocate for a pragmatic, whole-system approach to decarbonising heat. He emphasises that there is no single solution, and that progress will depend on a balanced mix of technologies, supported by clear policy, long-term investment and a resilient energy system. A central part of his work is ensuring the UK has the capability to deliver the transition. His vision for the sector is based on three core principles: smoothing barriers to consumer adoption and building confidence in the transition; supporting domestic manufacturing through a competitive environment that supports UK jobs, economic growth and community impact; and investing in the necessary skills and training for the future to build a sustainable workforce.

Alongside his role at Vaillant, Henrik plays a leading role in the wider industry. He is Chair of the Heating and Hotwater Industry Council (HHIC) and Vice President of the Energy and Utilities Alliance (EUA) and is an active contributor to organisations including the Heat Pump Association UK (HPA), the British Electrotechnical and Allied Manufacturers’ Association (BEAMA) and the Confederation of British Industry (CBI). Through these roles, he champions a collaborative approach to the energy transition, bringing together industry, government and consumer groups to deliver a more sustainable, secure and resilient heating system.

He holds an MSc (Econ) in strategic planning and marketing from Copenhagen Business School.

His work spans the full project lifecycle, from securing high-voltage grid connections and negotiating power purchase agreements with major counterparties, through to structuring the project financing and capital raises that take assets from conception to financial close.

bio.html: Carsten Hansen is Director of Power Markets, EMEA at Lightsource bp and a senior energy executive with more than 25 years of experience in global power markets. Having held leadership roles at Northland Power, Centrica and Barclays, he brings deep expertise in commercial strategy, energy origination,  and asset optimization. At Lightsource bp Carsten leads the regional power markets strategy, advancing innovative offtake agreements and maximising the value of the company’s growing renewable energy portfolio of solar and energy storage projects across EMEA. He holds a Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering from Imperial College and an MBA from IMD

Adil Hanif heads the Sustainable Markets unit in EBRD's Climate Strategy and Delivery group. The Sustainable Markets unit is responsible for the EBRD's support to policy makers on the use of market-based mechanisms and market reforms to deliver zero-carbon power systems. It is home to the EBRD’s Renewable Energy Market Accelerator programme, which supports EBRD’s countries of operations to create enabling frameworks that will attract private sector investment, including the design and implementation of incentive schemes. To date, incentive schemes supported by the EBRD have led to over 14,000 MW of capacity being awarded. Adil is an economist by training and previously worked in microeconomic consulting advising private and public sector clients.

bio.html: Enrique is a Senior Lead for Energy Strategy on Google's EMEA Infrastructure team. He is responsible for data center deployment, developing energy and power strategies, securing energy supply, and structuring Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) for Google's data centers.

Dominique Silva is the Marketing Leader EMEA at Trane Technologies. Dominique is responsible for developing and executing marketing strategies that support the company’s growth and reputation through thought leadership, advocacy and demand generation. As a mechanical engineer with a passion for innovation and impact storytelling, Dominique has served in a variety of roles in the company, including product management, brand management and enterprise innovation. Her proudest achievements include launching several innovative heat pump product lines in Europe.

Dominique is a prominent voice, and host of the Trane Technologies podcast – Healthy Spaces – where she actively drives critical conversations on modern data center design, scalable cooling strategies, and environmental impact. 

Dominique graduated from the Technical University of Lisbon with a master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering. She also holds a dual-degree MBA from the University of Manchester and Kelley Business School.

Harry is part of the Sustainable Investing team at Robeco, an asset manager with £350bn in assets under advice in public markets. He focuses on engagement with high impact companies on climate change and biodiversity, advocating for improved management of material sustainability issues to aid financial performance and positive societal outcomes. He is heavily involved in collaborative industry initiatives and developing IP to assist clients with their sustainable investing challenges. Prior to Robeco Harry worked in sustainable investing and active ownership at Columbia Threadneedle, BMO and the Church Commissioners for England, having started his career as a management consultant.

Deepa Venkateswaran is the Chief Strategy Officer at SSE overseeing Group Strategy and Energy Economics. She is a member of the NESO's independent stakeholder group. Deepa has over 20 years of experience in Utilities & Clean Energy built across a career spanning management consulting and equity research. Prior to joining SSE in September 2026, Deepa was the Head of European Utility & Clean Energy research at Bernstein (an independent premier equity research firm) where she joined in 2013. While at Bernstein, Deepa has advised institutional investors and authored several equity research notes on European Utilities including SSE as well as thematic research on grids, renewables, decarbonisation and the energy transition. Deepa was ranked number 3 in Extel's 2026 investor survey. Prior to Bernstein, Deepa was a Junior Partner at McKinsey focussing on the Utilities sector helping corporates on topics across the utility value chain on strategy & growth, corporate finance, regulation of networks and power market design. She was also a member of the leadership team in McKinsey’s Utilities & Regulatory practices. Deepa holds an MBA with Distinction in Finance from the London Business School and is also a qualified Chartered Accountant, having trained at Arthur Andersen/ E&Y in India.

Vishal Gulati is the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) at GE Vernova Financial Services, where he provides financial leadership and drives the strategy and execution of the business’s global finance activities.

With over 25 years at GE and GE Vernova, Vishal has held senior finance and operations leadership roles across the U.S., Europe, and Asia. His experience spans serving as Finance Leader for Global Markets in London, CFO for Restructuring, Strategic Ventures, and Insurance Group at GE Capital International, and General Manager of GE Financial Markets in Dublin. He has also served as CFO of GE Capital UK, Business Development Finance Leader for GE Capital APAC, and CFO of Capital Markets for US Retail Finance.

Prior to GE, Vishal spent six years in public accounting advising clients in financial services, manufacturing, and M&A. He holds a Bachelor of Commerce (Honors) from Delhi University and is a Chartered Accountant from The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.

Kaity is responsible for Wayve’s partnerships strategy, business development and commercialization of AV2.0. She is building the ecosystem of private, public and government partners that will shape the development and deployment of our technology. She leads functions that include commercial strategy, business development, partnerships, marketing, legal, and public policy.

Kaity is a seasoned leader in the autonomous vehicle industry with extensive experience in developing early-stage partnerships and operationalising autonomous ride-hailing trials. Before Wayve, she led business processes and partnerships at Aptiv (now Motional) and Alphabet’s Waymo.

Kaity holds a bachelor’s degree and an MBA from the University of Michigan.

Seb Henbest is Group Head of Climate Transition at HSBC, supporting the development, evolution and integration of the bank’s climate strategy and working with its most emissions-intensive clients to accelerate their transition to a net-zero future. He joined the bank in 2022.

Prior to this he spent 14 years at BloombergNEF, most recently as Chief Economist. In that role he oversaw the firm's energy economics group and energy transition scenario analysis and was lead author of BNEF's flagship publication, the New Energy Outlook. Before that he was Director of BNEF's Europe, Middle East and Africa division and Head of Research for BNEF in Australia, establishing the firm's Sydney offices in 2009.

Seb is a senior spokesperson on the energy transition, speaks regularly at industry conferences and events, and is quoted widely in print media.

He has appeared as an expert commentator on ABC TV, Sky News, BBC, Bloomberg TV and ABC Radio.

In 2012 he gave evidence to House of Representatives Economics Committee in Australia on the pricing dynamics of linking Australia's Carbon Price Mechanism with the EU Emissions Trading Scheme.

He is a 2015 Rex J Lipman Fellow and was previously an advisor to the GCC region Clean Energy Business Council.

Seb studied physics and theoretical astrophysics at Adelaide University and atmospheric science at Monash University in Australia, before moving to the UK where he read International Relations at Clare Hall, Cambridge, specializing in emissions trading and environmental markets.

Marie Carlsson is a passionate driver of electromobility with over a decade of experience shaping sustainable solutions for transport industry and public transport industry. She works currently as VP Electromobility Business Solutions at Volvo Trucks, a global leader in sustainable transport solutions. Marie enables transport companies and their customers to transform operations and accelerate the transition to more sustainable solutions. In her role she connects stakeholders across the ecosystem and bridges knowledge cross industries, technologies, and value chains to deliver scalable, tangible impact. Marie is committed to advancing the electrification of transport and inspiring next generation of sustainable mobility leaders.

Marie has extensive experience in global automotive, logistics and public transport industries, holding several senior commercial and customer centric positions in the Volvo Group. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration and Service Management.

bio.html: Erik Strømsø is the CEO and co-founder of BW ESS. Before this role, he was a Senior Equity Partner and head of Asia Pacific at Pareto Securities, a leading energy-focused investment bank.

Sonia Dunlop is CEO of the Global Solar Council, where she represents the world's solar PV industry with respect to policy-makers, other sectors and the media. She previously worked for SolarPower Europe, Solar Energy UK and the RE-Source Platform. Previously she was for five years part of the senior management team of global climate politics think tank Third Generation Environmentalism (E3G) and worked for the COP26 Glasgow organising team in the UK government. She also spent five years in the European Parliament in Brussels working on renewables policy. She has expertise in solar PV, development finance, renewables, digitalisation of energy, Multilateral Development Banks climate finance and corporate Power Purchase Agreements. Sonia speaks fluent English, French and Italian as well as basic Dutch, Spanish, Portuguese and Chinese, has two children and is based in London.

Maria Rapin is CEO of Nephila Climate, which provides risk transfer solutions aiming to accelerate the energy transition. As CEO she is responsible for the business strategy and management and serves as Chair of the Investment Committee. Maria joined Nephila in 2015 and in 2020, she took on her current role as CEO of Nephila’s Climate strategy and broadened the opportunity beyond parametric weather products. She began her career at Swiss Re Capital Markets, working in New York and London structuring, selling and trading catastrophe bonds. Prior to joining Nephila, she was portfolio manager for insurance-linked investments at SCOR Investment Partners in Paris. Maria is a graduate of The George Washington University in Washington, DC where she studied International Business and Information Systems.

Jordi Francesch is Global Head of Clean Energy at Nuveen Infrastructure, leading the firm’s clean energy equity infra business globally. Based in London, he sets strategic direction for Nuveen’s clean energy equity investment strategy, overseeing investment execution, asset management, product development, and investors relations across the platform. He chairs the investment committee of the different funds under management in Nuveen’s Clean energy equity funds and provides strategic direction across value creation, power markets and asset management strategies across the portfolio. Jordi sits on the Board of Directors of UK regulated entities and several platforms such as Verdian Power, BNZ and JVs, overseeing governance for the wholly owned projects and regularly reporting to the management committees, investors and non-executive boards.

Jordi joined Nuveen infra as part of its acquisition of Glennmont Partners, where he previously served as Global Head of Asset Management and Chief Risk Officer for the Clean energy business. In that role, Jordi led his team providing strategic direction to the lifecycle of the portfolio, leading on any material contractual challenges, assisting with acquisitions and their incorporation into the portfolio, overseeing governance for the wholly owned projects and regularly reporting to the management committees, investors and non-executive boards. He has more than 24 years’ experience in the energy sector, 11 of which has been spent in renewables. Before joining Nuveen Infrastructure, Jordi spent 10 years at Royal Dutch Shell, the world’s second largest independent energy company. Jordi holds B.A.s in Finance & Business Administration and Economics respectively from Universitat Pompeu Fabra (Catalonia, Spain) and an MSc in Environmental Economics from University of London.

He has more than 23 years’ experience in the energy sector, 11 of which spent in renewables. Before joining the team, Jordi spent 10 years at Royal Dutch Shell, the world’s second largest independent energy company.

Jordi holds B.A.s in Finance & Business Administration and Economics respectively from Universitat Pompeu Fabra (Catalonia, Spain) and an MSc in Environmental Economics from University of London.

Terry Yuan is currently General Manager of Overseas ESS Business at Sunwoda. He has 20 years of international business experience, 16 of which have been dedicated to the renewable energy sector. He is responsible for planning and implementing overseas marketing strategies to position Sunwoda as a globally leading energy solution provider. Drawing on extensive knowledge and experience in energy storage systems and the broader energy market, as well as a strong network of suppliers and customers, he carries out his work accordingly.

She is passionate about ensuring an energy transition where wind power plays a significant role, enabled by efficient policy frameworks and supported by sustainable supply chains.
